## Find anything in three commands

Paths are relative to the skill folder (`.claude/skills/kosif-superpowers/`); `repo` tools run from the repository root.

```bash
python3 scripts/hub.py find "<the task in the user's words>"   # tools + powers + guides, Arabic or English
python3 scripts/hub.py tool <tool-id>                          # commands, requirements, safety, tests
python3 scripts/hub.py doctor                                  # what runs on this machine now
```

Any MCP client can ask the same questions: `python3 scripts/kosif_mcp.py` (read-only stdio server; `python3 scripts/hub.py mcp-config`).
Machine-readable: [manifest.json](../manifest.json) (everything below as JSON) and [data/tools.json](../data/tools.json) (the editable registry).

### Think, ideate and write / التفكير والأفكار والكتابة

Thinking engines, idea generation, sizing estimates and writing-quality checks.

| tool | what it does | first command | guide | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor-gate` | Compares a text before and after a rewrite (English and Arabic) and reports every factual anchor that was dropped or added (quotes, numbers in digits or words, currencies, months, weekdays, emails, URLs, paths, @handles, versions, ratios/times and must-keep names), returning PASS or REVIEW_REQUIRED. | `python3 scripts/anchor_gate.py --before proofs/general-writing/pairs/en_before.txt --after proofs/general-writing/pairs/en_after_drift.txt --text` | [humanizer.md](humanizer.md) | tested-here |
| `architecture-sizer` | Computes a deterministic back-of-envelope capacity estimate (average and peak RPS, minimum replicas, logical and replicated storage in bytes and GiB) from caller-supplied traffic and hardware assumptions, using exact decimal arithmetic. | `python3 scripts/architecture_sizer.py --daily-requests 86400 --peak-factor 5 --payload-bytes 1000 --retention-days 7 --replica-rps 100 --target-utilization 0.5 --copies 2` | [community-source-atlas.md](community-source-atlas.md) | tested-here |
| `invention-lab` | Turns one problem statement into a reproducible, ranked JSON list of falsifiable engineering ideas (16 TRIZ-style inventive methods × 4 lenses), each with a hypothesis, test, success metric and rejection threshold. | `python3 scripts/invention_lab.py methods` | [creativity.md](creativity.md) | tested-here |
| `tell-scan` | Scans English and Arabic (MSA and Egyptian) prose for stock 'AI-sounding' writing habits and tool leftovers, and reports each hit with its line, strength and an overall verdict (EDIT/REVIEW/LOOK/LEAVE/CLEAN). | `python3 scripts/tell_scan.py proofs/general-writing/samples/en_ai.txt` | [humanizer.md](humanizer.md) | tested-here |
| `think` | Turns thinking procedures into checkable text scaffolds. It picks a reasoning level (L0–L6), writes a task contract, ranks 63 mental models, drafts a backcast plan, builds an idea matrix from catalog powers, scores a weighted decision with sensitivity, runs a Monte-Carlo Fermi estimate and flags weak wording in a draft. USIP v5.4 adds four reasoning tools: it ranks eight reasoning modes for a task, updates a belief by likelihood ratios with a halve/double sensitivity, gives a GO/PIVOT/KILL/HOLD verdict from thresholds written in advance, and builds a claim-to-evidence ledger for a draft. USIP v5.5 adds four intelligence scaffolds: it detects a request's deliverable kind and sorts its slots into filled, assumed, asked (within the level's question budget) and blocking; checks a task DAG and computes its order, optimistic and pessimistic critical path and one-way doors; prints the quality bar of twelve deliverable kinds and gives PASS, FAIL or INCOMPLETE from answers; and prints the recovery ladder for a FusionForge error class with an attempt budget. The Pro pass prints 4, 8 or 12 intelligence passes (standard, deep, max), each with a question, the artifact to write and a falsifier that forces a redo, plus a task-fitted council of 5, 9 or 15 personas, two reasoning modes and three mental models. | `python3 scripts/think.py ladder "design a 30-day plan for a course launch"` | [A24-reasoning-modes-decision-gates.md](protocol/A24-reasoning-modes-decision-gates.md) | tested-here |
| `council` | Plans a five-member adversarial council for a request (Visionary, Skeptic, Builder, Audience, Guardian, each with its own evidence lane and a specialisation from the brief's deliverable), writes every member's prompt for each round (independent positions, cross-examination, scored vote), validates and fingerprints each answer, refuses secrets, and computes a Borda verdict with recorded dissent, warnings and a SHA-256 receipt. It never calls a model: Claude runs the members as separate agents, or labels them COUNCIL_SIMULATED. With --seats N (5-15) it seats a deterministic, task-fitted council from data/council_100.json: 100 unique invented personas, 20 per evidence lane, each with a detailed character, three superpowers, three signature questions, a declared blind spot, the evidence it demands and a counterpart; --personas picks them by id, --full seats all 100 on explicit request, councils above nine see a digest of the other answers, and the personas command lists, searches or shows the roster. | `python3 scripts/council.py plan "اعمل ريلز دعاء" --dir out/demo/council --options A,B,C` | [A13-pro-council.md](protocol/A13-pro-council.md) | tested-here |
| `see-pro-cognitive-gate` | Validates cognitive-packet metadata: bounded SEE method packs, typed capability handoffs, genuinely distinct A/B/C planning keys, evidence provenance, deterministic numeric checks, cross-company isolation, and receipt-based truth for Full Pro execution and Council reviewer counts. | `python3 scripts/see_pro_cognitive_gate.py --self-test` | [A12-see-pro-cognitive-fusion.md](protocol/A12-see-pro-cognitive-fusion.md) | tested-here |
| `capability-mindmap` | Orders every superpower by task stage (understand, plan, create, refine, assemble, verify, deliver), builds stage plans for any request and 12 ready task maps with Mermaid flowcharts, and audits same-name groups, twins, cross-superpower look-alikes and pairs to develop together. | `python3 scripts/capability_mindmap.py build` | [capability-mindmap.md](capability-mindmap.md) | tested-here |
| `charter-ingest` | Deterministically parses the user's charter roster (sectors «القطاع N», numbered entries with الدور/المهام/الخصائص) into data/experts_500.json (kosif.experts-index.v1): every entry keeps its role, tasks and traits, maps by keywords to catalog families, and is flagged (boilerplate traits, duplicate_of, sensitive consent/regulated). Refuses unless 50 sectors × 10 entries (or --allow-partial) and refuses credential-like text. The council's plan consults it as an index; no persona runs, votes or counts as evidence. | `python3 scripts/charter_ingest.py roster.txt --out data/experts_500.json` | [A13-pro-council.md](protocol/A13-pro-council.md) | tested-here |
| `business-workflows` | Searches Futurepedia's business adoption index and 64 workflow playbooks (36 library + 28 creator), re-routes every step from the named third-party tool to what Claude can do in the session or to a connector, measures native coverage, and writes an Arabic runbook with approval gates for send, post, spend and recording. | `python3 scripts/business_workflows.py functions` | [A18-futurepedia-business-workflows.md](protocol/A18-futurepedia-business-workflows.md) | tested-here |
| `book-methods` | Searches 45 methods distilled in our own words from ten uploaded PDFs (lateral-thinking course, The Pragmatic Programmer, Jaynes's Bayesian framework, the Cambridge Handbook of Personality Psychology, an IFRS/ISA accounting skill report, the owner's KOSIF v8 prompt spec, Shawqi's diwan, two English coursebooks), and runs five helpers: seeded random-word provocation, a Bayesian posterior with a decibel evidence ledger, a prompt clarity/context/specificity gate, a journal-entry checker (balance, integer minor units, VAT, duplicates, bank-receipt-is-settlement) and a Big Five character card. | `python3 scripts/book_methods.py search "شخصية حوار"` | [A20-book-distilled-methods.md](protocol/A20-book-distilled-methods.md) | tested-here |
| `prompt-lab` | Makes the prompt-craft method runnable for eight kinds of prompt (system, agent brief, code, research, writing, LLM judge, image, video). build renders a kind's slots in order and turns every unfilled required slot into a question; lint scores a prompt out of 20 (required slots present, anti-patterns such as vague or shouted words, hype tokens and negative-heavy rules, in English and Arabic) with hard gates for a secret, a chain-of-thought request or undelimited pasted data; refine orders the fixes and prints the missing-slot skeleton; eval runs deterministic assertions on saved outputs and keeps a variant only when it beats the baseline with no regression; pairwise prints order-swapped judge prompts and counts only verdicts that agree in both orders, the way the owner's Jev service judges. | `python3 scripts/prompt_lab.py kinds` | [prompt-optimizer.md](prompt-optimizer.md) | tested-here |

It never downloads: with no model it prints the URL and asks the user to fetch it. | `python3 scripts/image_local_ai.py models --json` | [mosamem-arabic-image-editor.md](mosamem-arabic-image-editor.md) | tested-here |
| `prompt-pack` | Turns a list of prompts or a scene/story spec into PACK.md and pack.json: every English prompt in ONE fenced block (wrapped in dir="ltr" for RTL pages), the Arabic explanation outside it, and a per-engine suffix from data/prompt_engines.json (Midjourney V7 flags marked version-sensitive, generic image negative line, generic video 'No subtitles or on-screen text.'). The lint only warns (contradictions, unseparated subjects, studio/artist/brand names, quality hype, text-in-image, missing negative baseline) and never rewrites a word; credential-like values are refused. It calls no engine. | `python3 scripts/prompt_pack.py build prompts.json --out out/demo/prompts --engine midjourney` | [A17-story-scene-charter.md](protocol/A17-story-scene-charter.md) | tested-here |

### Sources and references / المصادر والمراجع

Find and fetch external references, media and repositories safely, with licences and rights recorded.

| tool | what it does | first command | guide | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `atlas-external-bridge` | Reads a local KOSIF Atlas index of third-party skills (plus an optional copyleft index) and prints stats or keyword-ranked matches with licence scope, risk flags and verdicts; with --skill-root it also reads each match's SKILL.md headings. It never executes anything. | `python3 scripts/atlas_external_bridge.py stats --index ./atlas_index.json --copyleft-index ./atlas_copyleft_index.json` | [sources.md](guides/sources.md) | tested-here |
| `atlas-body-audit` | Picks a bounded, topic-stratified sample of skills from a KOSIF Atlas index (plus an optional copyleft index), fetches each raw SKILL.md and up to N of its script files from the kosif-atlas repository, and scans them for review indicators (remote script execution, destructive shell, secret collection, prompt override, installs). It never executes anything and writes the fetched text, records.json and summary.json only to a private --out directory. | `python3 scripts/atlas_body_audit.py --index ./atlas-index.json --out ./out/atlas-audit-private --limit 200` | [atlas-reviewed-audit.md](atlas-reviewed-audit.md) | tested-here |
| `atlas-audit-synthesis` | Turns the private records.json from atlas_body_audit.py and a folder of REA static-analysis results into a metadata-only reviewed manifest (per skill: SKILL.md SHA-256, code files read, indicators, licence claim) and a short findings report. No third-party text is copied into the outputs, so the manifest can be committed as data/atlas-reviewed/manifest.json, which atlas_external_bridge.py reads to annotate search results. | `python3 scripts/atlas_audit_synthesis.py --records ./out/atlas-audit-private/records.json --rea-dir ./out/rea --manifest-out ./out/manifest.json --report-out ./out/atlas-reviewed-audit.md` | [atlas-reviewed-audit.md](atlas-reviewed-audit.md) | untested |

It can take a read-only viewport screenshot of one target in a fresh headless Playwright context that blocks off-host requests, downloads, service workers and saved cookies. | `python3 scripts/browser_scout.py doctor` | [sources.md](guides/sources.md) | tested-here |
| `creative-external-search` | Keyword-searches an offline index of 1,000 public GitHub repositories (video editing and processing, motion graphics, image and photo tools, computer vision, creative coding) and 1,000 creative websites extracted from curated awesome lists (design tools, motion graphics, AI image tools, creative coding, video production), and prints ranked JSON matches labelled metadata-only. | `python3 scripts/creative_external_search.py search "kinetic typography" --kind repo --top 5` | [REA_CREATIVE_DISCOVERY_2000_20261019.md](REA_CREATIVE_DISCOVERY_2000_20261019.md) | tested-here |
| `fetch-reference` | Discovers media URLs on a public web page (video and source tags, Open Graph and Twitter tags, JSON-LD, script text) or takes a direct file or an unencrypted HLS playlist. It downloads the media within a size cap into a git-ignored cache and measures it with ffmpeg (probe, contact sheet, scene cuts and dominant palette), plus a bilingual REPORT.md for STYLE.md. | `python3 scripts/fetch_reference.py https://example.com/page --list --json` | [reference-inspection.md](reference-inspection.md) | tested-here |
| `fetch-video` | Wraps yt-dlp to download one or many video or audio links for editing, with a format fallback chain, optional browser impersonation, a user cookies file and a quality cap. It can add an edit-safe H.264/AAC .safe.mp4 copy and writes a manifest.json with the file, duration, dimensions, frame rate, codecs, title, uploader and any license the site exposes. | `python3 scripts/fetch_video.py --doctor` | [video-download.md](video-download.md) | tested-elsewhere |
| `stock-fetch` | Downloads free stock clips by id or page URL without an API key: Pexels through its public download endpoint (a 302 to videos.pexels.com) and Mixkit through its free 720p file. It writes manifest.json with the page, file URL, licence name, link and terms, size, dimensions, frame rate and duration, can skip oversized files, and has a probe that reports which stock sources answer from the current machine. | `python3 scripts/stock_fetch.py probe` | [sources.md](guides/sources.md) | tested-here |
| `media-sources` | Lists and searches a fixed catalog of 100 stock, open-collection and texture websites and prints the legal prerequisites for a URL. It downloads a single asset through fetch_video.py only after explicit per-asset rights evidence is supplied, and records each download with its SHA-256 and rights in asset_rights.jsonl. | `python3 scripts/media_sources.py list` | [stock-media-100.md](stock-media-100.md) | tested-here |

| `source-scout` | Searches a curated offline registry of 31 reviewed GitHub repositories (plus a dated top-10 Python star snapshot) and returns ranked reference sources with licence, caution and code-reuse gates as JSON. | `python3 scripts/source_scout.py check` | [community-source-atlas.md](community-source-atlas.md) | tested-here |

### Software investigation / فحص البرامج

Lawful inspection of apps, binaries, installers and repositories (REA, Ghidra, triage, packing).

| tool | what it does | first command | guide | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `installer-triage` | Standard-library triage of Windows installers and desktop apps before REA. It identifies the installer family (NSIS, Inno, WiX Burn, Squirrel, InstallShield, MSI), UPX packing, Electron, .NET and the signature slot, and finds payloads hidden in PE resources. It also lists and fingerprints Electron asar bundles, unpacks payloads with 7-Zip or innoextract on request and maps each artifact to the matching REA command. | `python3 scripts/installer_triage.py scan ./setup.exe` | [rea-reverse-engineering.md](rea-reverse-engineering.md) | tested-here |
| `local-project-audit` | Performs a read-only static inventory of a local folder without executing anything and returns a JSON report of file counts, extensions, routes (source review, Ghidra/REA binary candidates, archives, media), regex indicators, SHA-256 hashes and zip-safety stats. | `python3 scripts/local_project_audit.py ./my-project` | [investigate.md](guides/investigate.md) | tested-here |
| `rea-bridge` | Opt-in bridge to the REA reverse-engineering CLI that stays within what the evidence shows. It checks Node and REA readiness, lists the 241 REA power records in the catalog (153 CLI commands, 76 MCP tools, 6 prompts and 6 KOSIF installer-triage additions) and plans an inspection without running it. Only with --authorized does it run one of 14 static local REA inspectors, saving the output to a new JSON file named by the caller. | `python3 scripts/rea_bridge.py doctor` | [rea-reverse-engineering.md](rea-reverse-engineering.md) | tested-here |
| `web-app-study` | Studies one public web page read-only: a logged-out headless Chromium with a fresh profile and background networking off (fresh profile, deleted afterwards), then REA captures the page, page-declared WebMCP tools, a screenshot and the public scripts, with SHA-256 receipts; optional bounded static JavaScript analysis. report turns a study folder into facts only: framework and versions, canvas/editor/realtime libraries, services inferred from storage key NAMES, WebMCP tools and page metrics, each with file-and-identifier evidence and never code. Written for the MagicPath study; runs on any desktop OS. | `python3 scripts/web_app_study.py doctor` | [magicpath.md](app-studies/magicpath.md) | tested-here |
| `rea-family-router` | Read-only router that maps one target keyword from a fixed 29-word list (dotnet, apk, har, firmware, sqlite and others) to one of 16 REA capability families, giving the upstream tool name and availability status. It also reports whether rea and node are on PATH. | `python3 scripts/rea_family_router.py list` | [rea-reverse-engineering.md](rea-reverse-engineering.md) | tested-here |
| `rea-owned-repo-batch` | Batch static REA analysis of the user's own JavaScript, TypeScript and HTML GitHub repositories. It reads a private inventory (made by rea_creative_research_atlas.py own), shallow-clones the smallest eligible repos under a size cap with git (depth 1, blob:none) and runs REA's analyze-javascript-application on each through node. Clones and evidence stay in a local private folder, and only counts are printed. | `python3 scripts/rea_owned_repo_batch.py --private-output "$HOME/kosif-private" --rea-cli ./node_modules/rea-agents/scripts/rea.mjs --max-repos 16 --max-size-kb 8000` | [REA_CREATIVE_DISCOVERY_2000_20261019.md](REA_CREATIVE_DISCOVERY_2000_20261019.md) | untested |
| `repository-capability-packer` | Inspects a local repository folder or source ZIP for languages, capability signals, license files and a per-file SHA-256 manifest. It packs a deterministic, filtered source ZIP plus a JSON capability-transfer report, leaving out build caches, archives, executables, audio and video, keys, databases and files whose names suggest secrets. Nothing is run, imported or installed. | `python3 scripts/repository_capability_packer.py inspect ./repo --out ./repo-report.json` | [repository-capability-transfer.md](repository-capability-transfer.md) | tested-here |
| `atlas-bulk-source-audit` | Audits an authorized local Atlas source sample and records evidence without executing third-party skill code. | `python3 scripts/atlas_bulk_source_audit.py --help` | [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) | untested |
| `atlas-deep-fusion` | Selects source-linked Atlas methods for review against an authorized local Atlas index. | `python3 scripts/atlas_deep_fusion.py --help` | [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) | untested |
| `atlas-review-summary` | Summarizes source-audit evidence and provenance for candidate Atlas methods. | `python3 scripts/atlas_review_summary.py --help` | [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) | untested |
| `atlas-reviewed-methods-v3` | Works with reviewed Atlas method records and their provenance. | `python3 scripts/atlas_reviewed_methods_v3.py --help` | [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) | untested |
| `atlas-transfer` | Converts reviewed Atlas records into KOSIF capability catalog data; writes files only when explicitly approved. | `python3 scripts/atlas_transfer.py --help` | [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) | untested |
| `differential-exam` | Scores a candidate run against a reference run folder by folder and file by file (<run>/<scenario>/<files>), comparing JSON and JSONL as data and other files as text after masking volatile values (UUIDs, timestamps, epochs, temp names, long hex ids, durations, named root paths and dropped keys). It seals an exam with SHA-256 hashes before the work starts and verifies the seal later, and its self-check refuses to trust the scorer until reference against reference scores 100%. Stdlib only; it runs nothing. | `python3 scripts/differential_exam.py seal ./exam --out ./exam-seal.json` | [codex-agent-harness.md](codex-agent-harness.md) | tested-here |

Output is deterministic, and it never touches the 30 hand-made motion chapters. --check reports stale, missing or orphaned chapters without writing. | `python3 scripts/build_chapters.py` | [maintain.md](guides/maintain.md) | untested |
| `catalog-evidence-audit` | Statically audits every power record in data/powers/*.json for duplicate ids, malformed records and proof-link coverage. It checks only whether local 'kosif-tool/...' references exist and counts the claimed statuses and proof scopes. | `python3 scripts/catalog_evidence_audit.py` | [claude-auto-local-first.md](claude-auto-local-first.md) | tested-elsewhere |
| `check-skill` | Validates the kosif-superpowers skill with 14 read-only checks: SKILL.md frontmatter, power records, proof paths, relative Markdown links, contents headings, generated chapters, the counts marker, model names, secrets and leaked session paths, evals/evals.json, the data/tools.json registry with its generated hub files, power-count drift in the entry docs, the USIP protocol structure (PROTOCOL.md core and references/protocol/), and the reference layout (every file under references/ in exactly one section of data/skill_layout.json). It can also run the routing evals, then prints a text or JSON report and exits 1 on any error. | `python3 scripts/check_skill.py` | [maintain.md](guides/maintain.md) | untested |
| `skill-layout` | Keeps the skill's reference files in order: data/skill_layout.json puts every file under references/ (and the entry documents) into exactly one of eleven sections in reading order. It builds the readable map references/LAYOUT.md, checks it like a trial balance (no unlisted, doubly listed or missing file, no stale map), says which section holds a file, and prints the git mv commands that would move each section to its planned folder. It never moves a file itself. | `python3 scripts/skill_layout.py build` | [LAYOUT.md](LAYOUT.md) | tested-here |
| `package-skill` | Validates the skill with check_skill.py, then zips it deterministically into kosif-superpowers.skill for upload to claude.ai. The archive has a single top folder and one SKILL.md, whose description is replaced by the ≤200-character claude_ai_description. dist/, caches, vendor/, evals/ and (with --lite) media are left out, and the finished archive is re-verified. | `python3 scripts/package_skill.py` | [README.md](../../../../README.md) | tested-here |
| `relabel-proofs` | Recomputes the proof_scope field of every power record from where its proof entries resolve on this machine (repo > session > archive > sibling > receipt > style > url > missing/none) and rewrites data/powers/*.json in place.
